records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side size check hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` for every upload type, dropping the per-type `max_${type}_size_kb` site setting that previously governed attachments and other non-image types. For `type === 'attachment'` (and any non-image type), sites with `max_attachment_size_kb` above or below 10240 now enforce the wrong limit: a 5MB attachment on a site allowing 50MB is rejected in the browser even though the server would accept it, and a site capping attachments at 2MB gets up to 10MB pushed to the server where it fails with a generic server error instead of the client-side message.

This makes the client-side size validation ignore site settings like `max_attachment_size_kb`, so non-image uploads (e.g., `type === 'attachment'`) will be incorrectly accepted/rejected in the browser relative to server configuration.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The API/URL download path hardcodes 10.megabytes, replacing SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb as the download cap, which silently removes the operator's configured limit for API uploads specifically. Admins who lower max_image_size_kb cannot bound API-URL downloads below 10MB, and those who raise it above 10MB have API downloads truncated where direct uploads succeed — a behavioral asymmetry between the two upload paths introduced without any stated requirement.
records.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL-download path changed from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, hardcoding the cap only for this path. This creates a verifiable asymmetry vs. other upload paths that still rely on `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and it prevents operators from enforcing a lower cap (or allowing a higher one) for API URL downloads.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff removes all server-side enforcement of the upload size limit for images: any size is accepted and merely downsized, so the max_image_size_kb setting no longer rejects anything. An authenticated user uploads a multi-gigabyte 'image' (extension check only, is_image? uses filename) via multipart; the request body is fully buffered to a tempfile before any size check, and ImageMagick then runs up to 5 passes over attacker-controlled bytes — disk-fill and CPU exhaustion DoS on every worker, since the previous behavior (create_for rejecting oversize files / FileHelper.download's byte cap) is bypassed for the normal upload path which never had a pre-save cap other than the site setting.
records.rationale: The controller now explicitly tries to process oversized image uploads instead of rejecting them: it adds a loop that runs up to 5 ImageMagick downsizes whenever `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...; OptimizedImage.downsize(...); attempt -= 1`). This means an attacker can submit a very large multipart upload that is fully written to `file.tempfile` before any size-based rejection in this method, and the server will then do up to 5 expensive image conversion passes over that attacker-controlled file. records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination, and the loop re-invokes it while tempfile.size is still over the limit — ImageMagick convert with identical input/output paths truncates the output mid-write. The tempfile becomes a corrupt or zero-byte file; the loop can spin all 5 attempts on an empty file (size never drops below limit), and the corrupted bytes are then passed to Upload.create_for and stored as the user's upload — attacker gets to serve arbitrary/truncated image data or a 0-byte upload recorded as valid.
records.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (same `from`/`to`) and does not check the return value. records.issue_text: [BUG] The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently shadows the first (width, height) definition, so every existing caller invoking downsize with separate width/height args now has its height argument interpreted as opts and opts dropped. Existing thumbnail-generation call sites pass e.g. downsize(from, to, 100, 200) — the height 200 lands in the opts hash, dimensions becomes '100x' or geometry built from the wrong values, and opts like allow_animation are ignored everywhere, producing wrong thumbnails and skipping animation guards for all other code paths in the app.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop overwrites the user's original uploaded image file in place before Upload.create_for, silently and irreversibly destroying the original-resolution data with no backup of the pre-resize bytes. The stored upload (and the original full-size image users get when clicking a lightbox) is a re-encoded, progressively-shrunk JPEG/PNG instead of what was uploaded; once saved, the original pixels cannot be recovered, and animated GIFs re-encoded with allow_animation: false lose their animation entirely even when the original was under a different intended use.

records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in the same module, and the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the first (from, to, max_width, max_height), breaking every existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments. Any call site outside this diff that invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) now binds the Integer height into opts, so opts[:allow_animation] inside optimize raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) and thumbnail generation crashes instead of producing a resized image.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so a failed ImageMagick convert is silently retried and then the oversize/corrupted file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. When convert_with fails (exitstatus != 0), it returns false with no exception and no log; the loop re-reads tempfile.size, retries 5 times, then falls through and uploads the original oversized file — and because downsize operates in-place (from == to), a partially-written failed convert can leave the tempfile corrupted, so the user's image is destroyed and replaced by an opaque generic upload error with nothing logged server-side.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Defining self.downsize a second time in the same module silently overrides the first definition, so the width/height-arity variant no longer exists and its callers crash. Any existing call site invoking downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height) now resolves to the dimensions-string version with max_height bound to opts (an Integer), and `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) — every such thumbnail-generation call 500s. Ruby has no method overloading; the first def is dead code that hides this.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client-side size cap is hardcoded to 10MB, decoupling it from the server's SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb in both directions. An admin who raises max_image_size_kb above 10MB has valid uploads rejected in the browser with a 'file too large' dialog naming a limit the server doesn't enforce; one who lowers it below 10MB gets no client hint and relies solely on the server error — the two enforcement points drift with no single source of truth.
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js`, the per-type limit `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` was replaced with a hardcoded `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` (and similarly `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` was replaced with `10 * 1024` for the 413 case). This makes the client-side size validation ignore site settings like `max_attachment_size_kb`, so non-image uploads (e.g., `type === 'attachment'`) will be incorrectly accepted/rejected in the browser relative to server configuration.
